A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BeeS study and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original DPO experiments, GPT-4-judged win rates, training dynamics, ablations, and failure cases in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations on TL;DR, HH, UltraFeedback, and its variants.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same pre-DPO training, margin calculation, Bayesian aggregation, and offline/iterative selection procedures. The new diagram's missing logarithm conflicts with the retained method definition; it does not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same SFT data, TL;DR, HH, UltraFeedback and Llama/Mistral variants, and AlpacaEval benchmarks are used. No dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Random, IFD/Low-Gap, external/implicit margin, and full-dataset comparisons retain the same membership. The iterative-DPO and SimPO, alpha-DPO, and beta-DPO comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same data counts, model configurations, training budgets, hyperparameters, decoding settings, judging procedures, and metrics. Iterative DPO still uses three rounds with 20k prompts and BeeS selecting 5k pairs per round.

E4.justification: The margin distributions, training-dynamics analyses, model/algorithm transfer studies, subset-size analyses, and small-beta failure cases are retained. The failure examples in v3 Figure 12 are relocated to v4 Figure 6, not newly added.

E5.justification: v4 checklist Question 7 newly states that experiments were not repeated and statistical-significance metrics were not reported. This adds run-status information absent from v3; it does not establish a reduction in runs.

E6.justification: Matched result tables and existing plots retain their values and findings. For example, BeeS's Llama-3-8B-Instruct UltraFeedback LC/WR remain 30.03%/30.46% in v3 Table 2 and v4 Table 3. Appendix results and failure examples also match.

T1.justification: The assumptions, shrinkage/inflation derivation, and equations (1)-(3) are unchanged. However, new Figure 1 expresses implicit reward as a policy probability ratio, omitting the logarithm retained in Section 3.2 in both versions. This introduces a limited mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning margin-based selection, Bayesian aggregation, data efficiency, and iterative DPO. The headline claims using 10% offline data and 25% online data remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an interpretation distinguishing preference learning from contrastive representation learning and emphasizing explicit, well-defined preferences. Existing interpretations of noise, small-beta instability, and the model-scale limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a source-code repository address in Section 4.1 and states in checklist Question 5 that TRL was used for all DPO experiments. Existing hardware, timing, hyperparameter, and processing details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Deng et al., 'Learning to double-check model prediction from a causal perspective,' as reference 8 in the new Section 4.2 discussion. Existing references and the main research positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section hierarchy remain intact. v4 adds a short interpretive passage, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist, while updating affiliations, correspondence information, and the conference header.

P2.justification: v4 adds workflow Figure 1 and notation Table 1, reflows and renumbers displays, and relocates the failure examples. Some appendix plots are resized, but the existing result graphics are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The new code-access pointer, TRL disclosure, explicit run-status statement, and notation table modestly improve reproducibility information and clarity. These gains are tempered by the missing logarithm in the new workflow figure. The empirical evidence and main derivation remain unchanged, limiting the overall improvement.
